title: Google Cogentic Autonomously Produces 6 Math Papers Led by Claimed Unconditional L[1/3] Integer Factoring Bound
aiSystem: Google Cogentic Multi-Agent Harness (Gemini 3.1 Pro / Gemini 4 Argon)
whyItMatters: Google Research’s Cogentic agent autonomously wrote 6 theory papers in one drop—led by a claimed unconditional L[1/3] worst-case integer factoring bound improving Lenstra & Pomerance’s 1992 rigorous L[1/2] record.
summary: On November 25, 2026, Google Research committed six autonomously written mathematics and theoretical computer science papers to GitHub under Apache 2.0, produced end-to-end by Cogentic (arXiv:2609.40324)—a multi-agent orchestrator pairing competing Gemini prover agents with adversarial verifier agents and a persistent verified ledger. The flagship 54-page paper claims a classical zero-error Las Vegas integer factorization algorithm running in unconditional worst-case expected time L_N[1/3, 10^5] (certifying prime factors via AKS), matching the heuristic General Number Field Sieve exponent without unproven hypotheses and breaking Lenstra & Pomerance’s 34-year-old rigorous L_N[1/2, 1] barrier from 1992. The same drop includes claimed advances on deterministic subexponential factoring, finite-field discrete logarithms, 2-player Nash equilibrium approximation, the 2014 square-root Log-Rank barrier, and the 1964 Edge Reconstruction Conjecture.
technicalHighlights: Flagship manuscript claims an unconditional zero-error Las Vegas factoring algorithm in expected time L_N[1/3, 10^5] and workspace L_N[1/3, 40], improving the 1992 Lenstra–Pomerance rigorous L_N[1/2, 1] bound.

Accompanying 5 autonomous papers claim progress on deterministic subexponential factoring, finite-field discrete logs, Nash equilibrium approximation, the Log-Rank conjecture, and the 1964 Edge Reconstruction Conjecture.
Built by Cogentic’s orchestrator–prover–adversarial-verifier pipeline without human intervention after the initial prompt, though practical RSA security is unaffected by the 10^5 constant.
caveats: Freshly posted unrefereed GitHub manuscripts without Lean formalization or independent number-theorist sign-off; the explicit 10^5 constant means practical RSA cryptography is unaffected even if the asymptotic proof holds up under expert scrutiny.

scoreRationale.foundational: If validated, removing unproven heuristics to prove an L[1/3] integer factoring bound breaks a 34-year cornerstone barrier in algorithmic number theory, alongside five other classical open problems.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates Google’s autonomous multi-agent proof-discovery architecture (Cogentic) competing head-to-head with OpenAI and Anthropic on flagship TCS and number-theory problems.
scoreRationale.verification: Marked down heavily because the six GitHub manuscripts are day-old unrefereed claims lacking Lean formalizations or independent expert review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Produced six full-length theory manuscripts autonomously from single prompts in a coordinated multi-agent batch.
